correctness.rationale: For any N-cycle, the second-smallest point has one negative return at t0; equality of complete signs under powering forces (u-1)t0=0 modulo p^k and at most p^(k-1) units. Base-p digit reversal makes comparison signs depend only on the first nonzero base-p digit of t; all multipliers u=1 modulo p preserve it. Both steps are proved for all p,k. Finite checker independently reproduces exact maximizers and exhaustive small cycles; those tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating periodic-orbit rigidity problem asks how much information remains in complete left-right signatures. Rather than another isolated composite counterexample, this all-prime-power extremal theorem quantifies maximal loss of recoverability among powers with a sharp N/p bound, supplying a structural p-adic reason and an explicit extremizer. This is a natural quantitative strengthening of the qualitative prime/composite divide; no application to arbitrary interval maps is claimed.
